title: Eleven Marks and One Standard
subtitle: 标准与准则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 标准与准则（语言与思维·标准与评价）
meta: 主题语境：标准与准则（语言与思维·标准与评价）　|　核心词汇：criterion　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 criterion 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 my teacher ① set a criterion that none of the entries could meet, and she said the setting was the whole of the marking. The ② criterion, meaning the standard and not the mark, ran to eleven words and stayed that short; criterion, she said, is the only thing in a competition that is judged by how few can satisfy it.

Every ③ criterion in that scheme had the same first clause, and the ④ criterion at the end, meaning the one she kept for the final round and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever questioned twice. Criterion, my mother said, is nine parts first clause and one part somebody willing to apply it; my teacher said the applying is the part that fills eleven words.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the criterion was the whole of the dispute, meaning the yardstick and not the standard. The ⑥ criterion, meaning the yardstick and not any of that, is the only thing in a dispute that everybody uses and nobody agrees on; criterion, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a standard and a yardstick. She said the yardstick is the part they remember.

By 1977 the ⑦ criterion had become a line in a handbook, and the handbook had become an argument about the first clause. The ⑧ criterion of the whole thing, my teacher wrote in February, was one entry and thirty years of applying; criterion, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to apply it. He said the applying was never mentioned.

The ⑨ criterion I remember is the one at the end, which she set in 1983 and is still described as the hardest in the school. A ⑩ criterion, my mother said in 1985, is the only thing that improves by being questioned; every criterion, she said, is a yardstick that has agreed to look like a standard. She said the yardstick was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 标准（指那条标准本身，与那些分数相对）
C. 固定搭配：set a criterion 设定标准
D. n. 标准（指那套方案里每一项）
E. n. 标准（指末尾那一项）
F. n. 尺度；衡量依据（抽象：用来衡量的那把尺）
G. n. 标准（指手册里提到的那一项）
H. n. 判据；准绳（抽象总称）

items.q: set a criterion that none of the entries could meet
The criterion, meaning the standard and not the mark
the criterion was the whole of the dispute
the criterion had become a line in a handbook
The criterion of the whole thing
A criterion, my mother said in 1985

answers.why: set a criterion 意为“设定标准”，1969 年老师设定了一条所有参赛作品都达不到的标准。
criterion 意为“标准”，指那条标准本身而不是那些分数，只有十一个词。
criterion 指那套方案里每一项标准，每一项都以同样的第一款开头。
criterion 指末尾那一项（她留给最后一轮的那一项），是唯一有人质疑过两次的。
criterion 意为“尺度、衡量依据”，父亲说那把尺就是那场争论的全部，指的是用来衡量的依据而不是那条标准。
criterion 为抽象用法，指用来衡量的那把尺而不是那条标准，是争论里人人都用、却无人达成共识的东西。
criterion 意为“标准”，指手册里提到的那一项，到 1977 年这条标准成了手册里的一行。
criterion 意为“判据、准绳”，老师二月写道，整件事的准绳是一件参赛作品三十年的适用。
criterion 意为“标准、准则”，我记得的是末尾那一项，她 1983 年设定，至今仍被说成全校最难的。
criterion 为抽象总称，母亲说一条标准是唯一会因为被质疑而变好的东西。
